steps.say: A circuit is a loop that electricity flows around. It needs a battery to push the electricity.

figure.alt: A battery and a lit bulb joined in a loop.

steps.say: Components are the parts of a circuit: batteries, wires, bulbs, buzzers, motors and switches.
The loop must be complete. If there is a gap, electricity cannot flow.

figure.alt: A battery and an unlit bulb with a gap in the wire.

steps.say: A switch opens and closes a gap. Closed means on, and open means off.

figure.alt: A battery, a lit bulb and a closed switch in a loop.

steps.say: In a single loop, one break stops everything. Check for loose bulbs and flat batteries.
Batteries are safe for experiments. Mains electricity from sockets can badly hurt you.

check.prompt: Why does this bulb not light?

figure.alt: A battery and an unlit bulb with a gap in the wire.

options.why: New bulbs work fine in a complete loop.
Extra wire is not the problem here.

options.text: There is a gap in the circuit.
The battery is the wrong colour.
options.why: Colour does not matter to a battery.

hints: Follow the loop with your finger.
Look for a place where the wire is broken.
check.explanation: There is a gap, so the loop is not complete and electricity cannot flow.

check.prompt: When a switch is closed, the circuit is complete and the bulb is ___.
hints: A closed switch has no gap.
Electricity can flow all round the loop.
What does the bulb do then?
check.explanation: A closed switch completes the loop, so the bulb is on.
